prompt:
Write 11 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1034; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment grew to many times the usual amount for this injury, with near-daily visits and new body areas added weeks after the crash.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: The insured reported a hit-while-turning-left collision at an intersection and the claimant's vehicle was struck on its driver side. The claimant has retained counsel, and all further contact is being routed through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: The police report and two independent witnesses place the claimant inside the vehicle at the time of impact, and the other driver's account matches the insured's description of the turn. Photos taken at the scene are consistent with the reported sequence.

Entry 3: Initial damage appraisal shows the impact damage is largely in line with the described collision. No prior damage to the vehicle has come to light in our records or in the photos reviewed.

Entry 4: The claimant reported a wrist fracture from the collision, which is a plausible injury for a force of this kind. The attorney submitted the initial medical summary and asked that the claim be handled on the bodily injury track.

Entry 5: The claimant gave the same account of the collision in the recorded statement and again in a follow-up call with the attorney present. Details of the sequence did not shift between conversations.

Entry 6: The driver is listed on the policy and the coverage was in force on the date of loss. Nothing in the underwriting file suggests the vehicle damage predates the coverage period.

Entry 7: Records show no earlier injury to the wrist or nearby body areas, based on the prior medical history the attorney provided and our database search.

Entry 8: Treatment has increased sharply, with visits now happening almost every day and several times the typical volume for a wrist fracture of this type. New body areas were added to the treatment plan several weeks after the crash.

Entry 9: The treating provider's notes list additional complaints in areas not mentioned in the first report. We have requested the complete records and an independent medical review to assess how these relate to the collision.

Entry 10: The adjuster discussed the escalating treatment pattern with the attorney, who said the claimant's care is following the physician's recommendations. We are awaiting the independent review before setting a reserve.

Entry 11: Current status is open pending the medical review. The liability picture remains clear, with the other driver accepting responsibility for the turning-left collision.
